synthesis_summary: Synthesis rebuilt for a practicing-oncologist reader with four-bucket tiering (established / contested / suspected / emerging). Foundation of 32 curated landmark PMIDs anchors the established tier. Additional extractions from the 2026-01-20 to 2026-04-21 Europe PMC backfill populate the suspected/emerging tiers. The 2026-05-16 update added two novel emerging findings: (1) TREM2+ myeloid spatial exclusion co-defines CRC ICI resistance with multi-checkpoint T cell exhaustion — quadruple blockade achieves >70% clearance even in MSS CRC preclinically (Mestrallet 2026, Cell Rep Med); (2) Pan-cancer spatial ecotype taxonomy recoverable non-invasively from plasma cfDNA (Liquid EcoTyper) with striking ICI-response associations in melanoma (Zhang 2026, Nature). The 2026-05-17 update adds two novel emerging findings: (3) STING agonists paradoxically expand immunosuppressive regulatory B cells (Bregs) via PI3Kg in pancreatic cancer — dual STING/PI3Kg compound (Nano-273) achieves 201-day median survival in orthotopic PDAC models (Li 2026, Nature Cancer); (4) KSR2 acts as a tumor-intrinsic metabolic checkpoint linking Ras scaffold signaling to anti-PD-1 resistance via Warburg-effect reprogramming (Ge 2026, Cancer Immunology Immunotherapy). The contested bucket explicitly flags where landmark findings have weakened: HLA LOH non-deterministic, B2M loss not uniformly resistance, microbiome taxa non-replication across geographies, Akkermansia non-monotonic, Bacteroidales sign-flip across CTLA-4 vs PD-1, TGF-B drugs clinically disappointing, bTMB failed prospectively, PBRM1 not replicated, IPRES underperformed, KEYNOTE-177 biphasic PFS + OS non-significance, WNT clinical signal weaker than mouse, IDO + pembro failed (ECHO-301), Snyder 2014 tetrapeptide signature not replicated. The 2026-05-19 update adds two novel emerging findings: (5) P2RX7 in tumor-infiltrating Tregs senses extracellular ATP and promotes Treg accumulation and CTLA-4-mediated suppression in lung cancer — T cell-specific P2RX7 KO and pharmacological inhibition improve tumor control in mice; human survival correlation confirmed (Santiago-Carvalho 2026, Cancer Immunol Res); (6) CysLTR1 (targeted by FDA-approved montelukast) programs tumor-promoting myelopoiesis — CysLTR1 blockade reprograms (not depletes) tumor myeloid cells and restores anti-PD-1 efficacy across five cancer types and in acquired-resistance models; human tissue and dataset validation (Zhang 2026, Nature Cancer). The 2026-05-27 update refines the contested microbiome taxa non-replication bullet: a melanoma-focused meta-analysis (Zhang 2026, Communications Medicine, n=678, 7 ICI cohorts) identifies Faecalibacterium and SCFA biosynthesis as the most reproducible cross-cohort microbiome features within melanoma, and suggests disease-specific functional pathway analysis outperforms pan-cancer taxon abundance — while Akkermansia remained non-monotonic even in this pooled dataset. Additionally, a phase 2 basket trial (Naing 2026, Cell Reports Medicine, n=154 rare cancers) confirms that pre-existing CD3+/CD8+ T cell infiltration and TME T cell signaling activity predict pembrolizumab benefit pan-cancer, with intermediate-infiltration tumors showing inducible recruitment capacity also deriving benefit (consistent with the established TME exclusion paradigm — confirms, no text change). The 2026-05-29 update adds four novel emerging findings and one refinement: (1) Cancer-induced nerve injury (CINI) promotes anti-PD-1 resistance via IL-6/IFN-β neuronal signalling that remodels the TME; PNI/CINI burden correlates with worse ICI outcomes in patients; anti-IL-6R (tocilizumab) rescues sensitivity in nerve-injured tumour models (Baruch 2025, Nature); (2) TMEM87A maintains Golgi apparatus pH homeostasis to suppress ferroptosis and confer ICI resistance; TMEM87A ablation sensitizes to anti-PD-1 in preclinical models; high TMEM87A IHC correlates with worse ICI outcomes in patients (Li 2026, Nature Cancer); (3) SpaceCat spatial multiplex imaging in 103 TNBC patients (TONIC phase 2 trial) shows spatial diversity and T-cell border infiltration outperform bulk PD-L1 IHC for predicting ICI response — spatial context of immune cell positioning, not abundance alone, determines outcome (Greenwald 2026, Nature Cancer); (4) GIV/Girdin endocytic adaptor controls PD-1 surface availability on tumour macrophages; GIV loss causes hyperprogressive disease under anti-PD-1; psychotropic drugs disrupting PD-1 endocytosis phenocopy GIV loss — defines a macrophage-intrinsic endocytic checkpoint as a distinct resistance axis (Mullick 2026, bioRxiv). Refinement: CD40 agonism can bypass B2M/JAK-LOF antigen-presentation resistance through myeloid reprogramming without cognate T cell-antigen recognition, as a trailing clause added to the established JAK1/JAK2/B2M LOF bullet (Zimmerman 2026, bioRxiv). The 2026-06-15 update adds two novel emerging findings (Europe PMC API unavailable; papers found via web search): (7) Mesenchymal (MES) GBM transcriptional subtype predicts improved ICB survival (n=181 patients) via high HLA-I expression and T cell infiltration; non-MES transition is the molecular correlate of acquired ICB resistance — paradoxically, MES GBM is the ICB-responsive subtype (Ghannam 2026, Nature Cancer); (8) Intrathecal nivolumab (20-50 mg) is safe in leptomeningeal disease (IT-PD1/NOA-26 phase 1, n=30, 1 DLT at 40 mg) — first human proof-of-concept that CNS-compartment anti-PD-1 delivery bypasses blood-brain barrier pharmacokinetic resistance (Wick 2026, Nature Cancer). The 2026-06-19 update adds one novel emerging finding: Ago2 (Argonaute 2) post-transcriptionally suppresses STAT1-mediated IFN-γ signaling in NSCLC, driving an immunorefractory ICI-resistant phenotype; Ago2 deletion restores IFN signaling, promotes immune infiltration, and sensitizes LLC tumors to ICI (3.5-fold growth reduction at day 18); high Ago2 + low IFN signature correlates with worse ICI survival in NSCLC patients — repositioning RISC microRNA machinery as a tumor-intrinsic IFN signaling brake distinct from canonical JAK/STAT genetic LOF (PLOS Biology, June 18, 2026). Update 2026-06-29: BET bromodomain inhibitors (BETis) reinvigorate exhausted CD8+ T cells from lung cancer malignant pleural effusions by activating the MYC-ODC1 polyamine biosynthesis axis; scRNA-seq shows shift from terminal toward progenitor-like exhausted T cells; ODC1 inhibition abolishes the effect; the proximate mechanism is metabolic (polyamine pool expansion) rather than direct epigenetic reversal of TOX or NFAT — identifying polyamine biosynthesis as a new axis orthogonal to existing checkpoint and exhaustion-reversal strategies (Nature Immunology, June 2026). Update 2026-07-13: Three novel emerging findings added (Europe PMC API unavailable; papers found via web search): (9) Gut microbiome-driven MHC-II restoration in MSS CRC colon cancer cells overcomes PD-1 resistance and limits metastasis in preclinical models — bridges microbiome and antigen presentation axes in the canonical ICI-refractory indication (bioRxiv, June 30, 2026); (10) Single-cell multi-omics in HNSCC maps neutrophil state heterogeneity; neutrophil-activating therapy (NAT) induces distinct anti-tumoral states; ICAM1 marks ICI-responsive neutrophil states; elevated TAN density in cold tumors correlates with poor ICI prognosis (Gao et al. 2026, bioRxiv July 2, 2026); (11) Immune cell-intrinsic STING drives paracrine tumor ferroptosis via TBK1→cPLA2→arachidonic acid→ACSL4 K426 lactylation in CRC; STING agonist + anti-PD-1 synergize via this relay; mechanistically orthogonal to existing IFN-γ→IRF1→AGPAT3 ferroptosis axis (PNAS, June 30, 2026). Update 2026-07-14: One novel emerging finding added (Europe PMC API unavailable; paper identified via web search): (12) Diet–microbiome synergy is the mechanistic basis for the obesity paradox in ICI response — across 12 custom mouse diet models, ICI sensitivity correlates with diet-driven gut microbial ecosystem features rather than body weight or metabolic dysfunction per se; dietary switching or human-to-mouse FMT restores ICI sensitivity, decoupling the benefit from adiposity; identifies dietary modification as a tractable ICI-sensitization strategy complementary to FMT — upgrades diet from observational correlate to mechanistically supported intervention target in the microbiome literature (Desharnais et al. 2026, Nature, July 8, 2026). Update 2026-07-16: Three novel emerging findings added (Europe PMC API unavailable; papers identified via web search): (13) COMPASS pan-cancer concept bottleneck transformer uses 44 interpretable immune concepts from bulk RNA-seq to predict ICI response across cancers and treatment regimens; validated in multiple independent cohorts — bridges single-marker biomarkers (PD-L1, TMB) and spatial transcriptomics approaches for pre-treatment ICI response triage (Shen et al. 2026, Nature Medicine, July 3, 2026); (14) PID1 maintains immunosuppressive TAM identity by limiting oxysterol production — PID1 loss upregulates LDL receptor, driving oxysterol generation that switches macrophage fate to antitumoral phenotypes; pan-cancer human TAM expression correlation confirmed; mouse genetic data establishes causal role and sensitization to ICI — a new oxysterol-mediated macrophage fate axis orthogonal to existing myeloid reprogramming strategies (Zheng et al. 2026, Nature Cancer, June 16, 2026); (15) mKRAS-VAX (pooled mutant KRAS peptide vaccine targeting six KRAS mutations: G12D/V/R/C/A, G13D) combined with nivolumab + ipilimumab meets safety and immunogenicity primary endpoints in phase I (n=13, pretreated metastatic MMRp/MSS CRC); KRAS-specific T cell responses in 8/12 evaluable patients — directly addresses the core ICI-resistance mechanism of MSS CRC (low neoantigen burden) by supplying shared KRAS neoantigens; clinical activity signals in an indication where PD-1 has uniformly failed as monotherapy (Wang et al. 2026, Nature Communications, ~June 25, 2026). Update 2026-07-21: Three novel emerging findings added (Europe PMC API unavailable; papers identified via web search): (16) Tumor-cell P2RY2 senses immunotherapy-induced extracellular ATP to drive COX1/COX2-PGE2 immunosuppression — a positive-feedback adaptive resistance circuit that amplifies with each round of ICI-mediated cell death; P2RY2 inhibition reverses resistance to CAR-T, TCR-T, checkpoint blockade, and TIL therapies simultaneously in CRC, pancreatic, and melanoma preclinical models; anti-P2RY2 mAb enhances ex vivo killing of patient tumor cells by melanoma patients’ own immune cells — one of few mechanisms offering pan-modality sensitization (Hu et al. 2026, Immunity); (17) Tumor-derived GABA activates GABBR on granulocytic MDSCs to suppress antitumor T cells via the CAT2-L-arginine-NOS2 axis in GBM, but exclusively in female mice; GABBR antagonism extends survival in female but not male GBM models — a sex-specific neurotransmitter-myeloid immunosuppressive axis with implications for sex-stratified ICI trial design in GBM (Pathak & Deneen 2026, Nature Cancer); (18) Citraconate (itaconate isomer) is depleted from exhausted/hypoxic CD8 T cells; its loss drives stemness collapse and ferroptosis via the PDE1A/C-cAMP-PKA-ALOX5 axis; supplementation potentiates ICI in preclinical models; lower ALOX5/PDE1A expression correlates with less exhaustion and better ICI responsiveness in patients — an orthogonal metabolite-depletion vulnerability in exhausted T cells with a patient-level biomarker pair ready for prospective validation (Liu et al. 2026, Science Immunology). Update 2026-07-25: Two novel emerging findings added (Europe PMC API unavailable; papers identified via web search): (19) Tumor progression hijacks thymic central tolerance via CCR9-dependent pDC recruitment — CDP-pDCs migrate to the thymus and delete tumor-reactive developing T cells via MHC-I/II; CLP-pDCs suppress thymopoiesis via IFN-α; CCR9 deficiency enhances antitumor immunity in syngeneic mouse models. A systemic immune evasion axis entirely outside the TME, mechanistically orthogonal to all TME-based resistance nodes, with the implication that checkpoint blockade cannot rescue T cells that were never generated (Wang, Kato, Katakai 2026, Science Advances); (20) Common TP53 mutations (G242V, S258I) in CRC selectively retain mTORC1-suppressive function despite losing canonical activities — sustained mTORC1 inhibition drives autophagy protecting tumor cells from IFN-γ/TNF-α-mediated apoptosis and conferring anti-PD-1 resistance; Trp53 deletion restores mTORC1, increases CD8+ TIL clonal expansion, reduces Tregs; mTOR activation or autophagy inhibition sensitizes to ICI; human CRC cell line validation of mTORC1 inhibitor gene-set regulation. Inverts the expectation that TP53 LOF is purely a growth disinhibitor — identifies autophagy as an active immune evasion mechanism in CRC with a tractable vulnerability for ICI combination (Labani-Motlagh & Lu 2026, Cell Death & Disease). Update 2026-07-30: Two novel emerging findings added (Europe PMC API unavailable; papers identified via web search): (21) MEK-dependent bioenergetic demand drives terminal CD8+ T cell exhaustion — chronic TCR engagement elevates protein synthesis via MEK, causing mitochondrial NADH accumulation, ROS production, and progressive mitochondrial dysfunction; MEK inhibition uniquely reduces nutrient uptake, reverses RNA Pol II CTD phosphorylation at exhaustion-associated loci while sparing memory gene transcription, and attenuates terminal exhaustion in vivo; reframes terminal exhaustion as partly driven by upstream bioenergetic overload upstream of TOX/chromatin-fixation circuitry, orthogonal to the BETi/ODC1 polyamine and citraconate axes; FDA-approved MEK inhibitors enable near-term clinical testing (Mitra et al. 2026, Immunity); (22) CARM1 (coactivator-associated arginine methyltransferase 1) is a TGF-β-regulated epigenetic checkpoint that selectively suppresses cDC1 antigen cross-presentation in tumors — CARM1 inactivation promotes cDC1 accumulation, activation, and cross-presentation; CARM1 inhibition enhances cDC1-mediated T cell priming in the context of a neoantigen vaccine; BATF3-Jun and RelA chromatin accessibility mechanism; TGF-β drives Carm1, revealing a parallel DC-intrinsic mechanism by which TGF-β silences tumor immunity independent of stromal exclusion; mouse + human ex vivo validation (Zhang, Wucherpfennig et al. 2026, Science). In the July 22–31, 2026 window, four novel findings were added across three runs (Jul 25, Jul 30, Jul 31). Two this run: (1) TLS plasma cells in NSCLC generate citrullinated-protein antibodies via PADI2 after PD-1 blockade (Cancer Cell 2026); (2) PROTEXI DC vaccine repurposes pandemic SARS-CoV-2 CD4 memory to amplify anti-tumor CD8 responses in mouse models (Nature Communications 2026). Update 2026-08-05: One novel emerging finding added (Europe PMC API unavailable; paper identified via web search): (23) TRAILshort, a dominant-negative TRAIL splice variant expressed by cancer cells, binds DR5 on T cells and recruits SHP-1 phosphatase to dephosphorylate ZAP-70 — directly disrupting TCR signaling and impairing T cell recognition of tumor cells; in humanized mouse models, TRAILshort promotes tumor persistence and antagonizes CAR-T cell therapy; blocking TRAILshort restores T cell activity; TRAILshort RNA is elevated in human neoplasms, viral infections, and autoimmune diseases. This reveals an entirely new function of TRAILshort beyond its known apoptosis-inhibitory role — it operates as a tumor-secreted, apoptosis-independent immunosuppressant via a DR5-SHP-1-ZAP-70 axis that is mechanistically orthogonal to every checkpoint (PD-1/PD-L1, CTLA-4, LAG-3, TIM-3) and resistance mechanism currently in the synthesis (Jalali et al. 2026, Journal of Clinical Investigation). Update 2026-08-06: One novel emerging finding added (Europe PMC API unavailable; paper identified via web search): (24) CCR7+ activated dendritic cells (actDCs) are required not only for naive CTL priming in tumor-draining lymph nodes but also for sustaining pre-activated CTL function within tumors themselves — genetic depletion of actDCs using novel mouse models abrogates both spontaneous and ICI-driven anti-tumor immunity in vivo; cDC1-derived actDCs support CTL priming via cross-presentation, cDC2-derived actDCs via cross-dressing in a cancer cell-type-dependent manner. Identifies actDC compartment sufficiency inside the tumor as a distinct resistance determinant: absence of actDC support within the TME causes ICI failure independently of T cell-intrinsic exhaustion. Mechanistically complementary to (not duplicative of) the TGF-β/CARM1 epigenetic suppression of cDC1 cross-presentation (Koufaki, Zelenay et al. 2026, Immunity). Mouse-only; clinical validation awaited. Update 2026-08-07: One novel emerging finding added (Europe PMC API unavailable; paper identified via web search): (25) PPARα activation reprograms the fibroinflammatory liver microenvironment (FILM) to restore GSDME-dependent pyroptosis and overcome anti-PD-1 resistance in HCC — FILM suppresses GSDME-mediated pyroptosis in HCC tumor cells and drives immune exclusion; PPARα agonism reverses both effects and synergizes with anti-PD-1 in syngeneic mouse models and patient-derived organoids. Positions PPARα (already an approved target in metabolic liver disease via fibrates) as a candidate sensitizer for HCC immunotherapy via fibroinflammatory stromal reprogramming; mechanistically distinct from all antigen-presentation, T cell exhaustion, IFN-γ, and previously described metabolic resistance axes (Chen, Xiong, Huang et al. 2026, Nature Communications).

top_claims.text: Pre-existing CD8+ T-cell infiltrate at the invasive tumor margin predicts pembrolizumab response in melanoma; the inflamed/excluded/desert taxonomy generalizes pan-tumor.
TMB predicts anti-PD-1 benefit in NSCLC (Rizvi 2015) and anti-CTLA-4 benefit in melanoma (Snyder 2014); pan-tumor generalization and threshold choice remain contested.
dMMR/MSI-H is the most reliable single ICI biomarker across histologies; basis of first tissue-agnostic FDA approval and of KEYNOTE-177 in 1L mCRC.
JAK1/JAK2 and B2M LOF cause acquired and primary anti-PD-1 resistance via disrupted IFN-γ sensing and MHC-I presentation; rare (<5%) but biochemically definitive.
PTPN2 loss in tumor cells sensitizes to ICI by amplifying IFN-γ/JAK-STAT response; now in clinical development.
KRAS-mutant NSCLC with STK11/LKB1 co-mutation is primary anti-PD-1 refractory despite TMB-intermediate/high status; used in NSCLC trial stratification.
PTEN loss drives ICI resistance in melanoma via PI3K-AKT activation and reduced T-cell infiltration.
TGF-β signaling in peritumoral fibroblasts drives T-cell exclusion (Mariathasan 2018 urothelial; Tauriello 2018 MSS CRC GEMM); biology established but clinical translation failed.
Response to PD-1 blockade depends on a stem-like Tcf1+PD-1+ CD8+ progenitor pool, not on reinvigoration of terminally exhausted effectors.
TOX is the master transcription factor of the exhausted CD8 chromatin state; necessary and sufficient for the exhaustion transcriptome/epigenome.
PD-1 + CTLA-4 combination improves PFS over single-agent PD-1 in advanced melanoma; largest relative benefit in PD-L1-negative tumors; durable OS at 6.5+ years.
First-line pembrolizumab monotherapy is standard for NSCLC with PD-L1 TPS ≥50%.
Ipilimumab established the durable-OS-plateau paradigm in metastatic melanoma (20–26% plateau at 10 years); nivolumab phase I extended the proof to NSCLC/RCC.
Antibiotic exposure around ICI initiation is associated with worse outcomes — the most robustly replicated microbiome observation.

HLA-I LOH is a selected immune-escape event in ~40% of NSCLCs (McGranahan 2017) but is NOT deterministic for ICI response — some HLA-LOH patients still respond depending on which allele is lost, tumor type, and residual presentation capacity.

Microbiome responder-associated taxa do not replicate across geographies. Gopalakrishnan (Faecalibacterium), Routy (Akkermansia), Matson (Bifidobacterium), Sivan/Vétizou mouse findings each identify different taxa. Meta-analyses (Lee 2022, McCulloch 2022) found no single taxon reliably predicts response.

TGF-β biology is clinically validated but TGF-β-pathway drugs (bintrafusp alfa, galunisertib, NIS793) have largely failed pivotal trials — INTR@PID lung 037 discontinued 2021. A textbook translational gap.
bTMB prospective validation failed. Gandara 2018 retrospective POPLAR/OAK signal did not confirm in prospective B-F1RST; bTMB is not broadly adopted.
PBRM1 LOF as ICI sensitizer in ccRCC did not replicate in CheckMate-009/010/025 (Braun 2020) and IMmotion analyses.
IPRES transcriptomic signature underperformed as an independent predictor; overlaps heavily with TGF-β/stromal signatures and adds little above CD8/PD-L1/TMB.
KEYNOTE-177 PFS was biphasic (~29% primary progression) and final OS did not reach statistical significance (HR ~0.74, crossover). dMMR is not a universal predictor even in 1L mCRC.
WNT/β-catenin clinical signal is weaker and more context-dependent than Spranger 2015 mouse biology predicted.
FMT from anti-PD-1 responder donors can rescue anti-PD-1-refractory melanoma (Baruch 2021 3/10; Davar 2021 6/15 with ~20% ORR). Surprising because refractoriness had been framed as tumor-intrinsic.
PD-1 on clonally expanding human T cells partially protects them from restimulation-induced cell death (in vitro). If replicated in vivo, complicates the release-the-brakes framing of anti-PD-1.
AARS1 catalyzes lactylation of PD-L1 at K280, blocking HUWE1 ubiquitination and stabilizing PD-L1; exogenous lactate paradoxically enhances anti-PD-L1 efficacy preclinically (unresolved paradox).
HILPDA-KLF5-driven lipogenesis palmitoylates PD-L1 at Cys272 and stabilizes membrane PD-L1; fenretinide engagement of TRIM21 degrades HILPDA and restores anti-PD-1 efficacy in breast cancer models.

deltaHED (germline + somatic HLA-I evolutionary divergence) predicts worse PD-1 outcomes despite higher TMB/neoantigen load across three retrospective cohorts. Inverts naïve HED prediction; needs prospective single-agent PD-1 validation.
Hypoalbuminemia causally drives ICI resistance via impaired macrophage arginine biosynthesis in LLC mice; TAM depletion or dietary arginine rescues anti-PD-1.
TROP2-claudin-7 tight junctions functionally exclude T cells from TNBC; reframes TROP2 from ADC target to barrier-mechanism target.
ATOMIC phase 3: adjuvant atezolizumab + mFOLFOX6 in stage III dMMR colon cancer, HR 0.50 for 3-year DFS (86.3% vs 76.2%); OS not yet mature.
KLRG1 nominated as novel inhibitory checkpoint in anti-PD-1-resistant melanoma; novel anti-human KLRG1 mAb reduces tumor progression in humanized KI mice via CD8/NK/γδ-T effects.
Anti-TIM-3 (TQB2618) + anti-PD-1 penpulimab achieves 52% ORR (1 CR, 10 PR) in 21 PD-1-pretreated classical Hodgkin lymphoma patients.
PKMYT1 inhibition with clinical-grade RP-6306 activates cGAS-STING and converts immune-cold CRPC to anti-PD-L1-responsive in preclinical models.
IFN-γ → IRF1 → AGPAT3 axis remodels lipids toward polyunsaturated ether phospholipids that sensitize to ferroptosis; higher AGPAT3 correlates with better ICI survival.
8-gene k-TSP + mucinous histology biomarker identifies 15% dMMR/MSI-H mCRC subgroup with 72% vs 14% 24-month PFS from anti-CTLA-4 addition to anti-PD-1 (HR 0.10). Retrospective; n=25.
LOAd703 + atezolizumab restores ICI-responsive immune signatures in 24 anti-PD-1-refractory melanoma patients; biomarker-level rescue in a hard population.
Single-cell spatial transcriptomics defines six niches stratifying neoadjuvant cSCC response better than PD-L1 IHC.
hMENA TGF-β-driven CAF 9-gene signature validated against OAK phase III in NSCLC as an ICT resistance marker.
M2 TAM-derived PGE2 via COX1/2 drives TIGIT upregulation on PD-1+ CD8+ in MSS CRC; COX2i, PGE2R antagonism, or TIGIT blockade restore anti-PD-L1 activity preclinically.

TREM2+ immunosuppressive macrophages are spatially enriched in T cell-excluded CRC niches and co-define ICI resistance with multi-checkpoint T cell exhaustion (TIM3/LAG3/TIGIT/PD-1); quadruple blockade (PD-1+CTLA-4+LAG-3+TREM2) achieves 100% clearance in dMMR and >70% in MSS CRC orthotopic models.

A pan-cancer spatial ecotype taxonomy (9 conserved SEs from 10M+ cells) can be recovered non-invasively from plasma cfDNA (Liquid EcoTyper); cfDNA SE levels in ~100 melanoma patients show striking associations with ICI response.

STING agonists paradoxically expand immunosuppressive regulatory B cells (Bregs) via PI3Kg in pancreatic cancer, partially offsetting STING-driven myeloid activation; dual targeting (SH-273/Nano-273) extends median survival to 201 days in orthotopic PDAC models, outperforming STING agonist or PI3Kg inhibitor monotherapy.

KSR2 (kinase suppressor of Ras 2) drives Warburg-effect glucose reprogramming in lung cancer, creating an immunosuppressive TME with depleted CD8+ TILs and enriched Tregs that confers anti-PD-1 resistance; KSR2 overexpression is sufficient and knockdown resensitizes; links oncogenic Ras scaffold signaling to metabolic immune evasion.

P2RX7 in tumor-infiltrating Tregs senses extracellular ATP in the lung tumor TME, promoting Treg accumulation and CTLA-4 upregulation; T cell-specific P2RX7 KO and pharmacological inhibition reduce Treg infiltration, increase CD4+ effector T cells, and improve tumor control; elevated P2RX7 correlates with worse survival in human lung cancer.

CysLTR1 programs tumor-promoting myelopoiesis that suppresses antitumor immunity and confers ICI resistance; blockade with montelukast (FDA-approved CysLTR1 antagonist) reprograms immunosuppressive myeloid cells into immunostimulatory ones and restores anti-PD-1 efficacy across five cancer types — including in acquired-resistance models — with human immune cell, tumor tissue, and patient dataset validation.

Cancer-induced nerve injury (CINI) promotes anti-PD-1 resistance via IL-6/IFN-β neuronal signalling that remodels the TME; perineural invasion burden correlates with worse ICI outcomes in patients; anti-IL-6R (tocilizumab) rescues sensitivity in nerve-injured tumour models.

TMEM87A maintains Golgi apparatus pH homeostasis to suppress ferroptosis and confer resistance to PD-1 blockade; ablation sensitizes to anti-PD-1 in preclinical models; high TMEM87A IHC expression correlates with worse ICI outcomes in patients.

SpaceCat spatial multiplex imaging in 103 TNBC patients (TONIC phase 2 trial) shows spatial diversity and T-cell border infiltration outperform bulk PD-L1 IHC for predicting ICI response; spatial context of immune cell positioning, not abundance alone, determines outcome.

GIV/Girdin endocytic adaptor controls PD-1 surface availability on tumour macrophages; GIV loss causes hyperprogressive disease under anti-PD-1; psychotropic drugs disrupting PD-1 endocytosis phenocopy GIV loss. Defines a macrophage-intrinsic endocytic checkpoint as a distinct resistance axis.

Mesenchymal (MES) GBM transcriptional subtype predicts improved overall survival on ICB (not standard chemoradiation) in 181 patients, associated with high HLA-I expression and greater T cell infiltration; transition from MES to non-mesenchymal state is the molecular correlate of acquired ICB resistance.

Intrathecal (intraventricular) nivolumab dose escalation (20-50 mg) is safe in leptomeningeal metastatic disease from solid tumors (IT-PD1/NOA-26 phase 1, n=30; 1 DLT at 40 mg); first human proof-of-concept that CNS-compartment anti-PD-1 delivery can bypass blood-brain barrier pharmacokinetics as a resistance barrier in leptomeningeal disease.

Tumor-intrinsic Ago2 post-transcriptionally suppresses STAT1-mediated IFN-γ signaling in NSCLC, creating an immunorefractory ICI-resistant phenotype; Ago2 deletion restores IFN signaling and ICI sensitivity in syngeneic models; high Ago2 + low IFN signature correlates with worse survival in NSCLC patients on ICI.

BET bromodomain inhibitors (BETis) reinvigorate exhausted CD8+ T cells from lung cancer malignant pleural effusions by activating the MYC-ODC1 polyamine biosynthesis axis, expanding intracellular polyamine pools and altering chromatin accessibility; scRNA-seq shows a shift from terminal toward progenitor-like exhausted T cells; ODC1 inhibition abolishes the effect.

Gut microbiome-driven MHC-II restoration in intestinal epithelial tumor cells overcomes ICI resistance and limits metastasis in MSS CRC preclinical models; connects gut microbiome to antigen presentation as a direct epithelial resistance axis in the canonical ICI-refractory indication.

Single-cell multi-omics in HNSCC reveals heterogeneous anti-tumoral neutrophil states induced by neutrophil-activating therapy (NAT); ICAM1 marks ICI-responsive neutrophil states and functions as an ICI response biomarker; elevated TAN density in cold tumors correlates with poor ICI prognosis.

Immune cell-intrinsic STING drives paracrine tumor ferroptosis in CRC via TBK1→cPLA2(Ser505)→arachidonic acid→ACSL4 K426 lactylation inhibition; STING agonist synergizes with anti-PD-1 via this immune-to-tumor ferroptosis relay; mechanistically orthogonal to autocrine IFN-γ→IRF1→AGPAT3 ferroptosis axis.

Diet–microbiome synergy is the mechanistic basis for the obesity paradox in ICI response: across 12 custom mouse diet models, ICI sensitivity correlates with diet-driven gut microbial ecosystem features (not body weight or metabolic dysfunction); dietary switching or human-to-mouse FMT restores ICI sensitivity, identifying dietary modification as a tractable ICI-sensitization strategy complementary to FMT.

COMPASS, a pan-cancer concept bottleneck transformer using 44 interpretable immune-concept features from bulk tumor RNA-seq, predicts ICI response and generalizes across cancer types and treatment regimens.

PID1 maintains immunosuppressive tumor-associated macrophage identity by limiting oxysterol production; PID1 loss switches TAM fate to antitumoral phenotypes via LDL receptor-driven oxysterol generation, improving anti-PD-1 efficacy.

Mutant KRAS peptide vaccine (mKRAS-VAX) targeting six KRAS mutations with nivolumab + ipilimumab meets safety and immunogenicity primary endpoints in phase I (n=13, pretreated metastatic MMRp/MSS CRC); KRAS-specific T cell responses induced in 8/12 evaluable patients.

Tumor-cell P2RY2 senses immunotherapy-induced extracellular ATP to drive COX1/COX2-PGE2 immunosuppression — an adaptive resistance loop that amplifies with ICI-induced cell death; P2RY2 inhibition reverses resistance to CAR-T, TCR-T, checkpoint blockade, and TIL therapies across CRC, pancreatic, and melanoma preclinical models; anti-P2RY2 mAb enhances ex vivo killing of melanoma patient tumor cells.

Tumor-derived GABA activates GABBR on granulocytic MDSCs to suppress antitumor T cells via the CAT2-L-arginine-NOS2 axis in GBM, but exclusively in female mice; GABBR antagonism extends survival in female but not male GBM models — a sex-specific neurotransmitter-myeloid immunosuppressive axis.

Citraconate (itaconate isomer) is depleted from exhausted/hypoxic CD8 T cells; its loss drives stemness collapse and ferroptosis via PDE1A/C-cAMP-PKA-ALOX5; citraconate supplementation potentiates ICI in preclinical models; lower ALOX5/PDE1A expression correlates with less exhaustion and better ICI responsiveness in patients.

Tumor progression hijacks thymic central tolerance via CCR9-dependent pDC recruitment: CDP-pDCs migrate to the thymus and delete tumor-reactive developing T cells via MHC-I/II antigen presentation; CLP-pDCs suppress thymopoiesis via IFN-α. CCR9 deficiency enhances antitumor immunity in syngeneic mouse models.

Certain TP53 mutations (G242V, S258I) in CRC selectively retain mTORC1-suppressive function, driving autophagy that shields tumor cells from IFN-γ/TNF-α-mediated apoptosis and confers anti-PD-1 resistance; mTOR activation or autophagy inhibition sensitizes mutant-p53 CRC to ICI.

MEK-dependent bioenergetic demand (elevated protein synthesis → mitochondrial NADH accumulation → ROS) drives terminal CD8+ T cell exhaustion; MEK inhibition reverses bioenergetic overload and attenuates terminal exhaustion in vivo while preserving memory-gene transcription.

CARM1 is a TGF-β-regulated epigenetic enzyme that selectively suppresses cDC1 antigen cross-presentation in the TME; pharmacological CARM1 inhibition enhances neoantigen vaccine-driven T cell priming and promotes cDC1 accumulation in tumors.

TLS-associated CD138+ plasma cells in NSCLC generate tumor-specific antibodies against citrullinated proteins (citrullinated vimentin as dominant antigen) after neoadjuvant PD-1 blockade; PADI2 ablation eliminates tumor reactivity; a PC-1 antibody CAR-T targets tumor and myeloid cells in vivo without off-target toxicity — identifying citrullination as a novel tumor antigen class and PADI2 as a druggable regulator of humoral antitumor immunity in ICI responders.

PROTEXI, a DC-based vaccine incorporating SARS-CoV-2 Spike CD4 helper epitopes, repurposes pandemic-acquired CD4+ T cell memory present in virtually the entire global adult population as a universal pre-formed helper signal, amplifying tumor-specific CD8+ cytotoxic T cell responses in melanoma and breast cancer mouse models with further enhancement by checkpoint immunotherapy combination.

TRAILshort, a dominant-negative TRAIL splice variant expressed by cancer cells, disrupts TCR signaling by binding DR5 on T cells, recruiting SHP-1 phosphatase, and dephosphorylating ZAP-70 — impairing T cell tumor recognition and blocking CAR-T cell activity in humanized mouse models; TRAILshort RNA is elevated in human neoplasms; blocking TRAILshort restores T cell immunity.

CCR7+ activated dendritic cells (actDCs) are required not only for naive CTL priming in tumor-draining lymph nodes but also for sustaining pre-activated CTL function within tumors themselves; genetic depletion of actDCs abrogates both spontaneous and ICI-driven anti-tumor immunity in vivo. Both cDC1- and cDC2-derived actDCs contribute via cross-presentation and cross-dressing respectively, in a cancer cell-type-dependent manner.

A fibroinflammatory liver microenvironment (FILM) suppresses GSDME-dependent pyroptosis in HCC tumor cells and drives immune exclusion, conferring anti-PD-1 resistance; PPARα activation reprograms FILM, restores GSDME-mediated pyroptosis, and synergizes with anti-PD-1 in syngeneic mouse models and patient-derived organoids.

mechanism_summaries.antigen_presentation: Established: JAK1/2 and B2M LOF cause acquired and primary resistance (rare but definitive); HLA LOH is common and positively selected; dMMR predicts response pan-histology; TMB association survives across dozens of cohorts. Contested: HLA LOH is not deterministic; β2M loss does not uniformly prevent response; TMB pan-tumor threshold debated; Snyder tetrapeptide signature failed to replicate. Suspected: deltaHED inverts naïve HED prediction. Update 2026-07-25: Thymic central tolerance hijacking via CCR9-dependent pDC recruitment is an entirely new systemic immune evasion axis (Wang, Kato, Katakai 2026, Science Advances) — operating at the level of developing T cell clonal deletion outside the TME; CCR9 deficiency restores antitumor immunity in mouse models. Emerging (2026-07-30): CARM1 is a TGF-β-regulated epigenetic checkpoint selectively suppressing cDC1 antigen cross-presentation in the TME; CARM1 inhibition promotes cDC1 accumulation, activation, and neoantigen vaccine-driven T cell priming; BATF3-Jun/RelA chromatin accessibility mechanism; parallel TGF-β-immune-suppression pathway distinct from stromal exclusion; mouse + human ex vivo validation (Zhang, Wucherpfennig et al. 2026, Science). TLS-associated plasma cells in NSCLC generate antibodies against citrullinated proteins after PD-1 blockade, with PADI2 as a druggable regulatory target (emerging, Cancer Cell 2026). Emerging (2026-08-06): CCR7+ activated dendritic cells (actDCs) are required not only for naive CTL priming in tumor-draining lymph nodes but also for sustaining pre-activated CTL function within tumors themselves; genetic depletion of actDCs abrogates both spontaneous and ICI-driven anti-tumor immunity in vivo; cDC1-derived actDCs support CTL priming via cross-presentation, cDC2-derived actDCs via cross-dressing in a cancer cell-type-dependent manner; identifies actDC compartment sufficiency inside the tumor as a distinct resistance determinant complementary to the TGF-β/CARM1 epigenetic suppression of cDC1 cross-presentation (Koufaki, Zelenay et al. 2026, Immunity).
mechanism_summaries.ifn_gamma_signaling: Established: JAK1/2/STAT1 LOF drives resistance; PTPN2 loss is the tumor-intrinsic ICI sensitizer (now in clinical development); IFN-γ has dual roles (driving adaptive PD-L1 resistance while also being the effector axis anti-PD-1 exploits). Emerging: IFN-γ-IRF1-AGPAT3 extends the axis into ferroptosis sensitivity. Emerging (2026-06-19): Ago2 post-transcriptionally suppresses STAT1 → ICI resistance in NSCLC; Ago2 deletion restores IFN signaling and ICI sensitivity (PLOS Biology 2026).
mechanism_summaries.tme_exclusion: Established: pre-existing CD8 infiltrate predicts response; inflamed/excluded/desert taxonomy; TGF-B signaling in CAFs excludes T cells. Contested: TGF-B drugs (bintrafusp alfa etc.) failed clinically despite compelling biology; IPRES under-replicated; WNT clinical signal weaker than mouse. Suspected: TROP2-claudin-7 barrier in TNBC; hMENA CAF signature (OAK-validated). Emerging: spatial niche stratification in cSCC; LOAd703 rescue in refractory melanoma; TREM2+ myeloid spatial exclusion + multi-checkpoint exhaustion co-define CRC resistance (quadruple combo shows preclinical efficacy even in MSS CRC); pan-cancer spatial ecotype taxonomy recoverable non-invasively from cfDNA (Liquid EcoTyper, melanoma ICI-response associations); STING agonists paradoxically expand immunosuppressive Bregs via PI3Kg in PDAC — dual Nano-273 compound overcomes both arms of suppression (201-day survival in orthotopic models); P2RX7 in Tregs senses extracellular ATP → Treg accumulation + CTLA-4 upregulation in lung cancer TME — pharmacological inhibition resensitizes (human + mouse evidence, Santiago-Carvalho 2026); CysLTR1 programs tumor-promoting myelopoiesis → ICI resistance — montelukast (FDA-approved) reprograms myeloid cells and restores ICI response across 5 cancer types including acquired-resistance models (Zhang 2026, Nature Cancer). Emerging (2026-05-29): CINI/PNI burden promotes ICI resistance via neuronal IL-6/IFN-β signalling — anti-IL-6R rescues (Baruch 2025, Nature); SpaceCat spatial diversity + T-cell border infiltration outperform PD-L1 IHC in 103 TNBC patients (TONIC trial, Greenwald 2026, Nature Cancer); GIV/Girdin endocytic adaptor controls macrophage PD-1 surface levels — GIV loss causes hyperprogression (Mullick 2026, bioRxiv). Emerging (2026-06-15): Mesenchymal GBM transcriptional subtype (HLA-I high, T cell infiltrated) predicts ICB survival in 181 patients; non-MES transition marks acquired resistance — paradoxically, MES GBM is the ICB-responsive subtype (Ghannam 2026, Nature Cancer). Emerging (2026-07-13): Single-cell multi-omics in HNSCC maps neutrophil state heterogeneity; NAT induces distinct anti-tumoral neutrophil states; ICAM1 marks ICI-responsive states; elevated TAN density in cold tumors associates with poor ICI prognosis (Gao et al. 2026, bioRxiv). Emerging (2026-07-21): Tumor-derived GABA activates GABBR on gMDSCs driving CAT2-L-arginine-NOS2 T cell suppression in GBM, exclusively in female mice; GABBR antagonism extends survival in female but not male GBM models — sex-specific neurotransmitter-myeloid immunosuppressive axis with implications for sex-stratified ICI trial design in GBM (Pathak & Deneen 2026, Nature Cancer).
mechanism_summaries.tumor_intrinsic_signaling: Established: STK11/LKB1 co-mutation drives NSCLC primary resistance; PTEN loss drives melanoma resistance. Contested: WNT/β-catenin clinical translation weaker than Spranger 2015; PBRM1 in ccRCC did not replicate. Suspected: AARS1-PD-L1 K280 lactylation (with unresolved paradox); HILPDA-KLF5-PD-L1 Cys272 palmitoylation (fenretinide rescues); NOTCH3-PVR-TIGIT in CRC. Emerging: PKMYT1-cGAS-STING activation in CRPC. Emerging (2026-05-29): TMEM87A maintains Golgi pH to suppress ferroptosis and confer ICI resistance; patient IHC correlation confirms clinical relevance (Li 2026, Nature Cancer). Emerging (2026-07-21): P2RY2 acts as the tumor-cell eATP sensor that drives COX1/COX2-PGE2 immunosuppression in an adaptive positive-feedback loop amplified by ICI itself; P2RY2 inhibition reverses resistance to four immunotherapy modalities (CAR-T, TCR-T, checkpoint blockade, TIL) in CRC, pancreatic, melanoma models; anti-P2RY2 mAb validated ex vivo with patient samples (Hu et al. 2026, Immunity). Update 2026-07-25: Certain TP53 gain-of-function mutants (G242V, S258I) suppress mTORC1 and drive autophagy-mediated resistance to IFN-γ/TNF-α apoptosis, conferring anti-PD-1 resistance in CRC — pharmacological mTOR activation or autophagy inhibition sensitizes (Labani-Motlagh & Lu 2026, Cell Death & Disease). Update 2026-08-05: TRAILshort (dominant-negative TRAIL splice variant) expressed by cancer cells binds DR5 on T cells, recruits SHP-1 phosphatase, and dephosphorylates ZAP-70 — directly disrupting TCR signaling independently of all checkpoint pathways; blocks CAR-T cell activity in humanized mouse models; TRAILshort RNA elevated in human neoplasms; blocking TRAILshort restores T cell activity; a novel tumor-secreted direct TCR signaling inhibitor, orthogonal to PD-1/PD-L1, CTLA-4, LAG-3, TIM-3, and all known resistance axes (Jalali et al. 2026, JCI).
mechanism_summaries.t_cell_exhaustion: Established: Tcf1+PD-1+ stem-like CD8 progenitor pool is the operative target of PD-1 blockade, not terminally exhausted effectors; TOX is the master regulator of exhausted chromatin state (but TOX ablation also impairs persistence). Suspected: PD-1 protects expanding T cells from RICD (in vitro only); T-intrinsic VISTA synergy with anti-CTLA-4. Emerging: KLRG1 as novel checkpoint; TAM-PGE2-TIGIT in MSS CRC; anti-TIM-3 + anti-PD-1 52% ORR in PD-1-pretreated cHL. Emerging (2026-06-29): BETi activates MYC→ODC1 polyamine biosynthesis axis in exhausted T cells from lung cancer MPEs; scRNA-seq shows shift from terminal to progenitor-like; ODC1 inhibition abolishes effect; mechanism is metabolic, not direct epigenetic reversal of TOX/NFAT. Emerging (2026-07-30): MEK-dependent bioenergetic demand drives terminal CD8+ T cell exhaustion via excessive protein synthesis → mitochondrial NADH accumulation → ROS → mitochondrial dysfunction; MEK inhibition reverses bioenergetic overload and attenuates terminal exhaustion in vivo; upstream of TOX/chromatin fixation; orthogonal to BETi/ODC1 and citraconate axes; FDA-approved MEK inhibitors available (Mitra et al. 2026, Immunity).
mechanism_summaries.metabolic: Established framework: adenosine, IDO, lactate, arginine, lipid mediators all modulate ICI; IDO + pembro failed (ECHO-301). Suspected: hypoalbuminemia causally drives ICI resistance via macrophage arginine (LLC mouse); PD-L1 post-translational regulation via lipid (HILPDA) and lactate (AARS1) inputs. Emerging: M2 TAM-PGE2-TIGIT axis in MSS CRC (combinatorial target set); KSR2 as tumor-intrinsic metabolic checkpoint linking Ras scaffold signaling to anti-PD-1 resistance via Warburg-effect glucose reprogramming — knockdown resensitizes. Theme: metabolic inputs operate on multiple substrates (killing capacity, PD-L1 stability, macrophage polarization, T cell exclusion). Emerging (2026-06-29): BETi-driven MYC→ODC1 polyamine biosynthesis reinvigorates exhausted T cells — cross-links to t_cell_exhaustion; ODC1 is a new immune-metabolic target in the T cell compartment. Emerging (2026-07-13): Immune cell-intrinsic STING drives paracrine CRC ferroptosis via TBK1→cPLA2→arachidonic acid→ACSL4 K426 lactylation; STING agonist + anti-PD-1 synergy via this relay; orthogonal to autocrine IFN-γ→IRF1→AGPAT3 ferroptosis axis (PNAS 2026). Emerging (2026-07-21): Citraconate (itaconate isomer) is depleted from exhausted/hypoxic CD8 T cells; its loss drives stemness collapse and ferroptosis via PDE1A/C-cAMP-PKA-ALOX5; citraconate supplementation potentiates ICI in preclinical models; lower ALOX5/PDE1A expression correlates with less exhaustion and better ICI responsiveness in patients — an orthogonal metabolite-depletion T cell vulnerability distinct from TME-extrinsic metabolic axes, with a ready patient biomarker pair (Liu et al. 2026, Science Immunology). Emerging (2026-08-07): PPARα activation reprograms the fibroinflammatory liver microenvironment (FILM) to restore GSDME-dependent pyroptosis and overcome anti-PD-1 resistance in HCC — PPARα agonism reverses FILM-driven immune exclusion and GSDME suppression; synergizes with anti-PD-1 in syngeneic mouse models and patient-derived organoids. PPARα fibrates are approved in metabolic liver disease, lowering the translational barrier for combination trials (Chen, Xiong, Huang et al. 2026, Nature Communications, DOI: 10.1038/s41467-026-75770-7).
mechanism_summaries.microbiome: Established: gut microbiota modulate ICI in mice; antibiotic exposure worsens outcomes (the most replicated human signal); composition differs between responders/non-responders in multiple cohorts. Contested: specific taxa (Faecalibacterium, Akkermansia, Bifidobacterium, Bacteroides) do not replicate across geographies; Akkermansia non-monotonic; Bacteroidales sign-flipped across CTLA-4 vs PD-1. Refined (Zhang 2026, n=678 melanoma): Faecalibacterium + SCFA biosynthesis pathway are the most reproducible cross-cohort features in melanoma specifically; suggests disease-specific functional pathway analysis is more reproducible than pan-cancer taxon-level analyses. Emerging (and reproducible!): FMT from responder donors rescues anti-PD-1-refractory melanoma (Baruch 2021, Davar 2021 — independent replication). Emerging (2026-07-13): Gut microbiome-driven MHC-II restoration in MSS CRC colon cancer cells overcomes PD-1 resistance and limits metastasis in preclinical models — new microbiome-antigen presentation axis in the canonical ICI-refractory indication (bioRxiv 2026). Emerging (2026-07-14): Diet-microbiome synergy is the mechanistic basis for the obesity paradox in ICI response — across 12 custom mouse diet models, ICI sensitivity tracks with diet-driven gut microbial ecosystem features, not body weight or metabolic dysfunction; dietary switching or human-to-mouse FMT restores ICI sensitivity, decoupling the benefit from adiposity; identifies dietary modification as a tractable ICI-sensitization strategy complementary to FMT (Desharnais et al. 2026, Nature, DOI: 10.1038/s41586-026-10750-x).
mechanism_summaries.clinical_intervention: Established: ipilimumab established the durable-OS paradigm; anti-PD-1 extended across histologies; KEYNOTE-024 set 1L NSCLC PD-L1 ≥50%; CheckMate 067 combo ipi+nivo in melanoma; KEYNOTE-177 1L dMMR mCRC. Contested: KEYNOTE-177 biphasic PFS + non-significant OS; bTMB prospective failure; pan-tumor TMB approval controversial; TGF-β and IDO combos failed. Emerging: ATOMIC adjuvant atezo in stage III dMMR (HR 0.50); 8-gene dMMR biomarker for anti-CTLA-4 addition (HR 0.10 in n=25 subgroup); LOAd703 in refractory melanoma; anti-TIM-3+PD-1 in cHL. Emerging (2026-06-15): Intrathecal nivolumab safe in leptomeningeal disease (IT-PD1/NOA-26 phase 1, n=30, 1 DLT at 40 mg); first human CNS-compartment anti-PD-1 delivery proof-of-concept (Wick 2026, Nature Cancer). PROTEXI DC vaccine repurposes SARS-CoV-2 CD4 memory as a universal vaccine helper signal in mouse cancer models (emerging, Nature Communications 2026).
